model_fitness.best_available_model: Patient-derived iPSC cortical/motor neurons heterozygous for a known SPG8 missense variant (e.g. N471D), paired with an isogenic variant-corrected line and an isogenic heterozygous WASHC5 null line as the haploinsufficiency comparator. Patient fibroblasts as a cheaper pre-screen. (INFERENCE: such lines are standard for dominant HSP genes, but I did not retrieve a publication reporting an existing SPG8 iPSC neuron line in this session — treat availability as unverified.)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the question asked: the decision is about allele dosage sign (dominant-negative vs haploinsufficiency) acting on WASH-complex-dependent endosomal actin and cargo sorting — a cell-autonomous, cell-intrinsic readout. EVIDENCE that the mutant protein is expressed and mis-functions with loss of interactors (Dictyostelium N471D, PMID:30061306) makes a cellular complex-function readout mechanistically on-target.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially. iPSC-derived cortical neurons are the correct lineage (layer-V-like projection neurons can be enriched), but in vitro axons are orders of magnitude shorter than a human corticospinal axon, so distal-axon vulnerability is only approximated.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: WASH complex integrity (co-IP of WASHC1/WASHC2/WASHC3/WASHC4 with strumpellin), endosomal F-actin patches on WASH-positive endosomes, retromer/WASH cargo surface levels and sorting (e.g. GLUT1, transferrin receptor, CI-MPR), lysosomal morphology/pH and degradative capacity, plus axonal readouts (axonal swellings, neurofilament/organelle transport, axon length).
model_fitness.important_limitations: No validated in vivo SPG8 model: heterozygous Washc5 knockout mice were reported to lack a motor phenotype (INFERENCE, PMID:26572744, recalled and unconfirmed), and no patient-missense knock-in mouse was identified. Cellular rescue cannot test delivery to layer V corticospinal somata, chronicity, or reversal of established axonal degeneration.

plan.critical_question: Does lowering the mutant WASHC5 allele improve WASH-complex function in human SPG8 neurons — and does lowering total WASHC5 make things worse? I.e. is the therapeutic sign dominant-negative (lower mutant) or haploinsufficiency (raise wild type)?
plan.proposed_experiment: Three-arm allele-dosage experiment in isogenic human neurons, using the ASO toolkit as a mechanism probe rather than a candidate drug. (1) Build/obtain a patient iPSC line with a heterozygous SPG8 missense variant plus two isogenic controls: variant-corrected, and heterozygous WASHC5 null (the haploinsufficiency mimic). Differentiate to cortical projection neurons. (2) Design 3-5 gapmer RNase-H1 ASOs with the mismatch positioned for single-nucleotide discrimination against the mutant site (design precedent: positional-chemistry allele-selective RNase-H ASOs with >100-fold discrimination, EVIDENCE PMID:23963702; stereopure SNP-selective ASOs, EVIDENCE PMID:39027419), plus a total-WASHC5 ASO and a non-targeting control. Verify allele ratio by amplicon NGS / allele-specific ddPCR on WASHC5 mRNA, requiring >=70% mutant knockdown with <=20% wild-type knockdown for the selective arm. (3) Read out WASH complex co-IP integrity, endosomal F-actin, cargo mis-sorting, lysosomal function and axonal swellings in: untreated patient, selective-knockdown patient, total-knockdown patient, corrected isogenic, heterozygous-null isogenic. (4) In parallel and cheap: long-read phasing of WASHC5 in all available SPG8 families to ask whether mutant alleles cluster on a few common haplotypes (workflow precedent EVIDENCE PMID:33209959; HD haplotype-coverage template EVIDENCE PMID:31708117) — this decides whether anything beyond an n-of-1 product is possible.
plan.model: Isogenic trio of human iPSC-derived cortical projection neurons (SPG8 missense heterozygote / variant-corrected / WASHC5 heterozygous null); patient fibroblasts as pre-screen for ASO allele selectivity.
plan.primary_readout: Allele-resolved WASHC5 mRNA levels (ddPCR/amplicon NGS) as the pharmacology gate; primary biology readout = WASH-dependent endosomal phenotype composite (endosomal F-actin patch density + a quantified mis-sorted cargo) with axonal swelling count as secondary.
plan.supportive_result: Patient neurons show a measurable endosomal/cargo phenotype vs corrected isogenic; mutant-selective knockdown moves it toward corrected; the heterozygous-null line is phenotypically normal and total knockdown does not rescue (or worsens). This is the dominant-negative signature.
plan.negative_result: Either (a) the heterozygous-null line reproduces the patient phenotype and total knockdown worsens it while selective knockdown gives no benefit — haploinsufficiency, kill mutant-lowering and redirect to raising wild-type strumpellin; or (b) no robust phenotype separates patient from corrected neurons at all — the assay, not the hypothesis, is the blocker, and no lowering program should advance until a quantitative neuronal phenotype exists.
plan.decision_enabled: Decides the sign of the therapeutic intervention and therefore whether to spend on an n-of-1 intrathecal ASO at all. Supportive + a workable haplotype structure → proceed to a patient-missense knock-in mouse and ASO CNS PK/knockdown in deep cortex (the real failure mode: HTT allele-selective ASOs had excellent in vitro selectivity yet no clinical benefit, EVIDENCE PMID:33209959). Supportive but every mutant allele private and unphaseable → accept n-of-1 only, with a single committed family. Negative → terminate the lowering program.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Same isogenic human iPSC cortical neuron trio (SPG8 missense het / corrected / WASHC5 het null). For RNAi specifically, add a heterologous selectivity assay first: dual-luciferase or HEK293 reporter co-expressing mutant and wild-type WASHC5 3'UTR/coding fragments to measure guide-strand allele discrimination cheaply before touching neurons. (INFERENCE; no published WASHC5 RNAi selectivity assay retrieved.)
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for allele discrimination and cytoplasmic mRNA silencing — appropriate because the target is a missense, non-splicing, cytoplasmically mature transcript (INFERENCE). Does not capture CNS biodistribution, which is this modality's actual weak point.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially — correct lineage, not correct axon length or in vivo layer-V context. Reporter cells capture none of the disease biology and are used only for chemistry triage.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Allele-specific knockdown ratio (reporter and endogenous), then the same WASH-complex/endosomal/lysosomal/axonal composite as the ASO arm.
model_fitness.important_limitations: No approved CNS siRNA and no retrieved SPG8 in vivo model means this modality cannot be de-risked on its principal liability (uniform silencing of deep layer-V corticospinal somata) in any currently available system. A patient-missense knock-in mouse would have to be built to test that, and ClinicalTrials.gov shows no RNA program in any HSP (EVIDENCE: NCT06948019; NCT05518188 are AAV gene addition in recessive AP4-HSP, out of scope).

plan.critical_question: Can a seed-positioned siRNA achieve a mutant:wild-type knockdown ratio good enough that an on-target wild-type loss penalty is tolerable — given that if WASHC5 is dosage-sensitive, wild-type knockdown is actively harmful?
plan.proposed_experiment: Run RNAi strictly as the second-choice reagent behind the ASO arm, and gate it on selectivity before any neuronal work. Step 1: tile 8-12 siRNAs with the variant nucleotide at guide positions 2-8 against a mutant/wild-type WASHC5 reporter pair; require >=10-fold allele discrimination and >=80% mutant knockdown at <=1 nM. Step 2: for passing guides, measure endogenous allele-resolved WASHC5 mRNA in patient fibroblasts by allele-specific ddPCR, and in parallel titrate a non-selective WASHC5 siRNA across a dose range in control neurons to define the wild-type-loss tolerance curve — i.e. how much wild-type strumpellin can be lost before the endosomal phenotype appears. Step 3: only if selectivity exceeds the tolerance margin, run the same three-arm isogenic neuron rescue described for the ASO arm with the lead di-siRNA architecture.
plan.model: WASHC5 allele-pair reporter cells → SPG8 patient fibroblasts → isogenic iPSC cortical neuron trio.
plan.primary_readout: Allele discrimination factor (mutant IC50 / wild-type IC50) placed against the independently measured wild-type-loss tolerance curve; then the endosomal/axonal rescue composite.
plan.supportive_result: A guide with >=10-20-fold discrimination whose wild-type knockdown at the efficacious dose sits well inside the tolerance margin, plus phenotypic rescue in patient neurons without rescue (or with worsening) from total knockdown.
plan.negative_result: Best discrimination is <5-fold, or the tolerance curve shows that even 20-30% wild-type loss produces an endosomal phenotype — the therapeutic window does not exist for RNAi. Drop the RNA modality and keep only the RNase-H ASO format, which has human CNS route precedent (nusinersen, tofersen; INFERENCE).
plan.decision_enabled: Decides whether RNAi is worth any further spend versus concentrating all resources on the ASO format. Critically, the tolerance-curve arm is informative no matter the result: it quantifies WASHC5 dosage sensitivity in human neurons, which is the same number that determines whether a wild-type-raising strategy is the right program instead. Note the honest sequencing: do not fund CNS siRNA chemistry or an in vivo knock-in mouse until the isogenic neuron experiment has fixed the sign of the intervention.
